transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Rachel Moore (Medisync CISO), Tom Alvarez (Head of IT), Priya Singh (Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Medisync is evaluating Redwood for inference hosting; main concerns are SOC 2 / ISO evidence, trust center access, RBAC/SSO (SAML / SCIM), audit/log retention, and encryption/KMS integration for PHI. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) options and data residency for EU. Agreed to share reports and controls mapping; follow-up to deep-dive KMS and private deployment checklist.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, I'll kick us off. Hi Rachel, Tom, Priya, can you hear us okay?
[00:05] Rachel: Yeah, loud and clear. Thanks Jamie.
[00:08] Jamie: Cool, so the purpose of today's call is a posture review across SOC 2 and ISO 27001, go over where Redwood's evidence lives, Trust Center access, and then Samir will cover some technicals around RBAC, SSO, audit logs, and KMS.
[00:20] Tom: Sounds good. We're mainly interested in understanding whether hosted can meet our compliance, or we need a private deployment. Also curious about data residency for EU patients.
[00:30] Samir: Great. Quick note, I'll interject with implementation detail. We do have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs, and a Trust Center that contains our reports and control documents. We'll talk about the difference between hosted and private in terms of tenancy and encryption keys.
[00:43] Priya: When you say Trust Center, is that a portal we can log into? We need read-only access for our auditors.
[00:48] Jamie: Yes, we can provide read-only Trust Center access to your security team. Often we do a temporary read-only link for auditors. We'll share the link after the call.
[00:55] Rachel: Good. Also, retention of audit logs is critical — we need 7 years per our policy for certain events. What is your default retention?
[01:05] Samir: Our standard retention for platform audit logs is 90 days in the hosted product, but for Dedicated and Private we can configure longer retention and export to your SIEM. There are also add-on packages for extended retention.
[01:17] Tom: OK, and how granular are the logs? We need user-level actions, API keys usage, resource creation, and kernel-level operations aren't necessary but we need model access records.
[01:27] Samir: We capture API request logs, actor identity (token or SSO principal), route/model used, timestamp, and high level response metrics. We mask payloads by default for hosted, but for Private we can retain full request/response logs if you control the environment.
[01:40] Rachel: Mask payloads — will that affect our ability to run forensics? For security incidents we need raw data sometimes.
[01:46] Jamie: For hosted we mask PII by default and store minimal payloads; for customers with stricter needs we recommend Private or Dedicated with a consent to retain detailed logs. We also support log exports to your S3 or SIEM (with encryption in transit).
[01:59] Priya: Encryption — does Redwood support customer-managed keys (CMK) or HSM integration? Our policy requires customer-controlled KMS for some data categories.
[02:08] Samir: Yes, we support KMS integration. For Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM. In Dedicated we offer optional CMK where you can control key rotation; hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys but we also have an option for BYOK for an enterprise plan. I should note sometimes the API call payloads are encrypted at rest using our keys unless BYOK is configured.
[02:30] Rachel: Can you outline which artifacts in the Trust Center map to specific ISO 27001 controls? We need a controls mapping document to attach to our audit evidence.
[02:38] Jamie: Absolutely — Samir will put together a controls mapping (Redwood control -> SOC 2/ISO control mapping) and we'll provide that as a spreadsheet. We'll include references to the sections in the SOC 2 report and the ISO statement of applicability.
[02:52] Tom: About SSO — we use SAML 2.0 with SCIM for provisioning. How mature is your SAML/SCIM integration and RBAC?
[02:59] Samir: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle. Our RBAC model allows role scoping at the org and project level; you can have admin, developer, observer, and custom roles. For Private and Dedicated we can lock down network-level access as well. There are some minor quirks around SCIM group mappings historically but we've got standard mappings documented.
[03:20] Priya: Do you support enforced MFA for all users?
[03:23] Jamie: Yes, we enforce MFA for Redwood admin accounts; for customer orgs we recommend enforcing MFA via SSO provider — you can require it in Okta/Azure AD and it will apply to all logins.
[03:34] Rachel: Data residency — we have EU data residency obligations for patient records. Can Redwood guarantee data stays in EU for hosted?
[03:41] Samir: We have region-specific hosting. For hosted customers you can choose EU region and we store data at rest in that region. For strict regulatory needs we recommend Private VPC or on-prem option where you fully control the network and storage. Note: backups and some global metadata may still touch control plane locations unless you choose Private with local control plane. We'll clarify that in writing.
[04:05] Tom: Are backups encrypted with CMK?
[04:08] Samir: Backups are encrypted; with BYOK or Private we can ensure backups use your KMS keys.
[04:13] Priya: How often do you do penetration tests and what's your vuln management cadence?
[04:17] Jamie: We do annual third-party pentests and quarterly internal vulnerability scans. Critical findings are remediated within an industry-standard SLA; we'll include our vuln management policy in the Trust Center docs.
[04:29] Rachel: Incident response — do you have an IR runbook we can see? We need to know notification windows and contact process for incidents affecting PHI.
[04:38] Jamie: Yes, IR runbook and playbooks are in the Trust Center. Our standard notification SLA for confirmed incidents is 72 hours for high-impact events; for critical we aim for immediate notification within 24 hours. We can also integrate with your incident channels.
[04:53] Samir: Quick technical aside on model fallback and data leakage: requests are passed to model runtimes — by default we don't use user data to train models, and we have contractual terms to that effect. For extra assurance, Private deployments keep data entirely within customer-controlled infrastructure.
[05:08] Tom: What about model provenance / third-party models — where do you source models and how do you attest to those?
[05:13] Jamie: We maintain a model catalog and verify performance characteristics. For compliance we can provide documentation on model sources, licenses, and our testing process. If you require only vetted models, we can limit your environment to a curated catalog or private model images.
[05:26] Priya: Are there any common gotchas customers run into during their audits?
[05:30] Samir: A few: mismatched scoping of services (they think hosted equals private), forgetting to document delegated controls to Redwood in their SOC documentation, and not capturing third-party subservice organization mapping — we usually provide a subservice org letter and a controls mapping to help.
[05:46] Rachel: For our auditors, we need a signed subservice org letter that states Redwood's responsibilities and boundary. Can you provide that?
[05:52] Jamie: Yes we'll provide a subservice org letter and an AUP summary.
[05:56] Tom: Contractually, do you support data processing addendums (DPAs) and EU SCCs?
[06:00] Jamie: Yes, we have a standard DPA and can execute SCCs; legal can accelerate for enterprise customers if needed. We'll share the DPA template.
[06:09] Priya: OK, a couple of specifics: 1) We need to validate that audit logs for admin actions are immutable and tamper-evident, 2) We need role separation for dev vs ops, 3) We need a controls mapping within 2 weeks.
[06:22] Samir: For immutability we support append-only logs and export to your S3 with object lock for extra tamper evidence. Dev vs ops separation is enforced via RBAC and project scoping. Controls mapping we'll prepare.
[06:35] Rachel: Do you have any customers in healthcare with similar requirements? References?
[06:40] Jamie: We do have several health customers; we can provide anonymized reference contacts and example artifacts — subject to NDA for some items.
[06:48] Tom: On the KMS front: what's the perf impact if we BYOK and rotate keys monthly?
[06:54] Samir: Little to no runtime impact; there's a short key-unwrap/verification at storage access. We have staged rotation support to avoid large reconnects. We'll include perf notes in the controls doc.
[07:07] Priya: One more on logging: can you provide a sample of the log schema so our SIEM mapping team can start work?
[07:12] Samir: Yes, we'll attach a sample logging schema and a mapping example for Splunk/Elastic.
[07:18] Jamie: Ok, sounds like we have clear asks. We'll share: SOC 2 Type II PDF + ISO 27001 certificate, Trust Center read-only access, controls mapping, logging schema, DPA template, and a private deployment checklist if you're thinking about VPC.
[07:33] Rachel: Great. For timing — we want controls mapping within two weeks and Trust Center access within a few days.
[07:40] Jamie: We'll aim for that. Action items noted.
[07:43] Priya: Any red flags on your side about our timeline? We're hoping to start a pilot in Q2.
[07:49] Jamie: Q2 pilot is feasible; for Private/on-prem it takes longer (~6-8 weeks provisioning), Dedicated can be quicker with reserved capacity. Hosted pilot can start immediately after contractual and security sign-offs.
[07:59] Tom: Pricing and procurement will follow; expect procurement questions around SLAs and support.
[08:04] Jamie: We'll work with legal and sales to give a procurement pack.
[08:08] Rachel: Ok thanks — one final question, are the SOC 2 and ISO certifications current?
[08:13] Jamie: Yes, SOC 2 Type II (covering the last 12 months) and ISO 27001 certified as of last year; we'll share cert dates in the docs.
[08:21] Priya: Perfect.
[08:23] Jamie: Alright, we'll recap next steps — Jamie to share reports and DPA; Samir to deliver controls mapping and logging schema; Priya to send Medisync questionnaire. We'll schedule follow-up for a 60-minute technical deep dive on KMS and VPC.
[08:38] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[08:39] Rachel: Thanks, bye.
[08:40] Jamie: Thanks all — talk soon.

End of transcript.
